answer: Give every agent economy one narrow inlet: a newcomer cannot transact until established peers attest a trail of verifiable, useful work it actually performed, with each attestation time-locked and publicly auditable. Reputation then accrues as a slow signal, never bought in bulk, so a whisper campaign of fresh fake identities cannot outvote earned history. An attacker wanting a thousand voting agents must pay a thousand times the real work cost, plus the waiting time, while honest agents keep their accumulated standing.
